microscope.definition: Magnifier of the image of small objects.

test-tube.definition: A slender glass or plastic container holds, combines, or warms small liquid samples in laboratory experiments.

beaker.definition: A flatbottomed jar made of glass or plastic.

flask.definition: A laboratory container with a narrow neck for holding liquids.

bunsen-burner.definition: A laboratory gas burner that produces a controllable flame and is used only with appropriate supervision and safety procedures.
bunsen-burner.exampleUsage: The Bunsen burner was demonstrated by the teacher under laboratory safety rules.

petri-dish.definition: A shallow round laboratory dish with a lid used to hold or grow samples in controlled conditions.
petri-dish.exampleUsage: The labeled Petri dish was kept in the laboratory incubator.

pipette.definition: Measuring instrument consisting of a graduated glass tube used to measure or transfer precise volumes of a liquid by drawing the liquid up into the tube.
pipette.exampleUsage: The researcher selected a calibrated pipette for transferring the specified liquid volume.

graduated-cylinder.definition: A narrow glass or plastic container has numbered marks for measuring liquid volume with reasonable accuracy.

funnel.definition: A wide-topped tool narrowing to a tube, used to direct material into a container.

tongs.definition: A tool with two arms used to grip or lift objects without holding them directly.
tongs.exampleUsage: The technician used suitable tongs to grip the sample holder.

safety-goggles.definition: Protective glasses worn to guard the eyes.

lab-coat.definition: Protective outerwear worn over ordinary clothes in a laboratory helps shield the wearer from spills and contaminating substances.

chemical.definition: A substance with a particular chemical composition.

element.definition: A substance made of atoms with the same number of protons that cannot be broken into simpler substances by chemical reactions.

compound.definition: A substance made of two or more different elements chemically bonded together.

molecule.definition: (physics and chemistry) the simplest structural unit of an element or compound.

atom.definition: (physics and chemistry) the smallest component of an element having the chemical properties of the element.

reaction.definition: (chemistry) a process in which one or more substances are changed into others.

acid.definition: A substance that can donate protons in an acid-base reaction; many aqueous acids have a pH below seven.

base.definition: A substance that can accept protons in an acid-base reaction; many aqueous bases have a pH above seven.

solution.definition: A homogeneous mixture of two or more substances.

crystal.definition: A solid formed by the solidification of a chemical and having a highly regular atomic structure.

gas.definition: A state of matter that expands to fill its container.

liquid.definition: A substance that flows and takes the shape of its container.

cell.definition: The basic structural and functional unit of living organisms.
cell.exampleUsage: The microscope image showed a cell from the prepared tissue sample.

bacteria.definition: Single-celled organisms that lack a membrane-bound nucleus.

virus.definition: (virology) ultramicroscopic infectious agent that replicates itself only within cells of living hosts.

dna.definition: The molecule that stores genetic information in cells and many viruses.

gene.definition: A region of genetic material associated with a functional product, such as a protein or RNA.

organism.definition: An individual living thing, such as an animal, plant, or bacterium.

tissue.definition: A group of cells organized to perform related functions in an organism.

organ.definition: A body structure made of tissues that performs a particular function.
organ.exampleUsage: The instructor described the heart as an organ made of different tissues.

photosynthesis.definition: A process in which plants and some other organisms use light energy to make sugars from carbon dioxide and water.

evolution.definition: Changes in inherited characteristics of populations across generations.

ecosystem.definition: A system formed by the interaction of a community of organisms with their physical environment.

specimen.definition: A bit of tissue or blood or urine that is taken for diagnostic purposes.

magnet.definition: (physics) a device that attracts iron and produces a magnetic field.
magnet.exampleUsage: The magnet attracted the iron object in the demonstration.

prism.definition: A transparent optical object with angled surfaces that can bend and separate light.

lens.definition: A transparent curved piece of material that bends light.

pendulum.definition: An apparatus consisting of an object mounted so that it swings freely under the influence of gravity.

circuit.definition: A connected path through which electric current can flow.

battery.definition: A device that supplies electrical energy through chemical reactions.

wire.definition: A thin metal conductor used to carry electric current in a circuit.

switch.definition: A device used to open, close, or change an electrical circuit.
switch.exampleUsage: The instructor identified the switch controlling the circuit.

pulley.definition: A simple machine consisting of a wheel with a groove in which a rope can run to change the direction or point of application of a force applied to the rope.
pulley.exampleUsage: The demonstration used a pulley to change the direction of the applied pull.

lever.definition: A rigid bar that pivots around a support to move or balance a load.

spring.definition: An elastic mechanical part that stores energy when stretched or compressed.

thermometer.exampleUsage: The thermometer showed the sample’s temperature.

hypothesis.definition: A tentative insight into the natural world.

experiment.definition: The act of conducting a controlled test or investigation.

observation.definition: The act of making and recording a measurement.

data.definition: A collection of facts from which conclusions may be drawn.

graph.definition: A visual display showing relationships between measured values or quantities.

chart.definition: A visual display organizing information or measurements.

conclusion.definition: A position or opinion or judgment reached after consideration.

variable.definition: A factor that can change or be varied in an investigation.

control.definition: A standard against which other conditions can be compared in a scientific experiment.

measurement.definition: The act or process of assigning numbers to phenomena according to a rule.

scale.definition: An instrument used to measure the mass or weight of an object.
scale.exampleUsage: The technician weighed the sample on the laboratory scale.

calculator.definition: A device used for doing mathematical calculations.
calculator.exampleUsage: She used a calculator to add the recorded measurements.
